items.title: Scene Planning
items.description: Pre-visualizing and documenting what each scene must accomplish before production.
definitions: Scene planning is the pre-production discipline of defining each scene’s narrative job, duration target, locations, talent, props, and coverage needs.
Prevent wasted shots by locking purpose, coverage, and dependencies early.
rules: Use when: Storyboard and shot-list phases
Do not use when: Spontaneous documentary moments that must stay reactive
decisionRules: Use when: Storyboard and shot-list phases
Avoid when: Spontaneous documentary moments that must stay reactive
troubleshooting: Avoid: Overplanning coverage that won’t cut
examples: Beat sheet → scene cards → shot list for 30s ad
professionalStandards: Scene planning is the pre-production discipline of defining each scene’s narrative job, duration target, locations, talent, props, and coverage needs.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Scene Composition
items.description: Arranging subjects, props, and space within a scene for clarity and hierarchy.
definitions: Scene composition is the spatial and visual organization of elements inside a scene so the primary subject and action dominate attention.
Make the scene’s story point readable in a single glance.
rules: Use when: Hero and demo scenes
Use when: Any framed storytelling beat
Do not use when: Intentional chaos as stylistic conflict—only when motivated
decisionRules: Use when: Hero and demo scenes
Use when: Any framed storytelling beat
Avoid when: Intentional chaos as stylistic conflict—only when motivated
examples: Product centered with lifestyle depth behind, logo readable
professionalStandards: Scene composition is the spatial and visual organization of elements inside a scene so the primary subject and action dominate attention.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Scene Continuity
items.description: Maintaining consistent details, screen direction, and logic across takes and scenes.
definitions: Scene continuity is the consistency of props, wardrobe, eyelines, lighting logic, and geography across cuts and related scenes.
Preserve believability so viewers stay in the story.
rules: Do not use when: Montage that intentionally jumps time/style
decisionRules: Avoid when: Montage that intentionally jumps time/style
troubleshooting: Avoid: Crossing line of action unplanned
examples: Coffee level and hand position matched across reverse angles
professionalStandards: Scene continuity is the consistency of props, wardrobe, eyelines, lighting logic, and geography across cuts and related scenes.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Scene Transition Planning
items.description: Designing how one scene hands off to the next visually and narratively.
definitions: Scene transition planning is the pre-design of cut, dissolve, match-cut, whip, or motivated camera moves that bridge scene purposes and emotions.
Keep narrative flow smooth and intentional across cuts.
rules: Do not use when: Single continuous take pieces
decisionRules: Avoid when: Single continuous take pieces
troubleshooting: Avoid: Hard cuts that break causality
examples: Match-cut pouring coffee to pouring product serum
professionalStandards: Scene transition planning is the pre-design of cut, dissolve, match-cut, whip, or motivated camera moves that bridge scene purposes and emotions.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Scene Timing
items.description: Allocating duration so each scene earns its screen time relative to the whole.
definitions: Scene timing is the deliberate budgeting of seconds (or frames) per scene according to narrative priority and platform length.
Protect hook and CTA while giving proof enough room.
rules: Do not use when: Untimed documentary observational scenes
decisionRules: Avoid when: Untimed documentary observational scenes
troubleshooting: Avoid: Hero scene eating CTA time
Avoid: Equal timing for unequal importance
examples: 15s: 2s hook, 5s problem, 5s demo, 3s CTA
professionalStandards: Scene timing is the deliberate budgeting of seconds (or frames) per scene according to narrative priority and platform length.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Scene Purpose
items.description: The single narrative or persuasion job a scene must accomplish.
definitions: Scene purpose is the explicit statement of what the audience must understand or feel after the scene—hook, problem, proof, desire, or action.
Keep every scene necessary and cuttable if it fails its job.
rules: Do not use when: Scenes kept only because they look expensive
decisionRules: Avoid when: Scenes kept only because they look expensive
examples: Purpose: prove waterproof → dunk demo scene only
professionalStandards: Scene purpose is the explicit statement of what the audience must understand or feel after the scene—hook, problem, proof, desire, or action.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Opening Scene
items.description: The first scene that hooks attention and establishes story world.
definitions: An opening scene is the initial designed unit of picture and sound that captures attention, orients context, and launches the story’s promise.
Stop the scroll and set narrative expectations.
rules: Do not use when: Seamless mid-funnel continuations
troubleshooting: Avoid: Slow logo-first opens on social
examples: Smash cut to broken phone screen then brand repair kit
professionalStandards: An opening scene is the initial designed unit of picture and sound that captures attention, orients context, and launches the story’s promise.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Closing Scene
items.description: The final scene that resolves emotion and delivers branding/CTA.
definitions: A closing scene is the terminal unit that shows the after-state, brand signature, and call to action with unambiguous hierarchy.
Land the memory and the ask cleanly.
rules: Use when: End of every conversion film
Do not use when: Cliffhanger teasers withholding close
decisionRules: Use when: End of every conversion film
Avoid when: Cliffhanger teasers withholding close
examples: Wide lifestyle resolve → logo + ‘Shop now’ hold 2s
professionalStandards: A closing scene is the terminal unit that shows the after-state, brand signature, and call to action with unambiguous hierarchy.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Hero Scene
items.description: A premium, high-attention scene that showcases the product or brand at peak desire.
definitions: A hero scene is a carefully lit and composed set-piece designed to maximize desirability and clarity of the product or brand moment.
Create the memorable visual peak of the commercial.
rules: Do not use when: Every scene—overuse dilutes impact
decisionRules: Avoid when: Every scene—overuse dilutes impact
troubleshooting: Avoid: Hero look without story context
examples: Slow orbit of watch face with rim light and clean void
professionalStandards: A hero scene is a carefully lit and composed set-piece designed to maximize desirability and clarity of the product or brand moment.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Product Reveal Scene
items.description: The moment the product is disclosed or unveiled as the answer.
definitions: A product reveal scene is a staged disclosure—visual, kinetic, or narrative—that introduces the product as the solution after context is set.
Convert built curiosity into clear product recognition.
rules: Do not use when: When product must be visible from frame one for compliance
decisionRules: Avoid when: When product must be visible from frame one for compliance
examples: Hands open box → product rises into key light
professionalStandards: A product reveal scene is a staged disclosure—visual, kinetic, or narrative—that introduces the product as the solution after context is set.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Lifestyle Scene
items.description: Scenes placing the product in aspirational or authentic daily life contexts.
definitions: A lifestyle scene depicts credible or aspirational use contexts that associate the product with identity, place, and emotion.
Help viewers imagine ownership and belonging.
rules: Do not use when: When claims require pure lab/demo clarity
decisionRules: Avoid when: When claims require pure lab/demo clarity
examples: Morning run with earbuds → coffee shop arrival calm
professionalStandards: A lifestyle scene depicts credible or aspirational use contexts that associate the product with identity, place, and emotion.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Demonstration Scene
items.description: Scenes that prove how the product works through visible action.
definitions: A demonstration scene is a purpose-built unit showing product function, feature interaction, or performance under observable conditions.
Deliver evidence that reduces risk and builds belief.
rules: Do not use when: When demo is legally restricted or unsafe to imply
decisionRules: Avoid when: When demo is legally restricted or unsafe to imply
examples: Wipe-clean demo of stain on fabric with timer overlay
professionalStandards: A demonstration scene is a purpose-built unit showing product function, feature interaction, or performance under observable conditions.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Comparison Scene
items.description: Scenes that contrast options, before/after, or competitor-class differences fairly.
definitions: A comparison scene stages two or more states or options so differences in outcome, quality, or ease are visually obvious and claim-safe.
Clarify superiority or fit without confusing or misleading.
rules: Do not use when: When comparative claims are legally barred
bestPractices: Same camera/light conditions when claiming parity tests
decisionRules: Avoid when: When comparative claims are legally barred
recommendations: Same camera/light conditions when claiming parity tests
examples: Split screen: manual spreadsheet vs automated dashboard
professionalStandards: A comparison scene stages two or more states or options so differences in outcome, quality, or ease are visually obvious and claim-safe.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Testimonial Scene
items.description: Scenes featuring real or portrayed customers validating the offer.
definitions: A testimonial scene presents a credible speaker’s experience—interview, VO, or UGC style—supporting a claim with human authenticity.
Transfer trust through social proof.
rules: Do not use when: When testimonials can’t be substantiated
decisionRules: Avoid when: When testimonials can’t be substantiated
examples: Founder-customer interview cut against product-in-use B-roll
professionalStandards: A testimonial scene presents a credible speaker’s experience—interview, VO, or UGC style—supporting a claim with human authenticity.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Background Selection
items.description: Choosing what sits behind action to support story without stealing focus.
definitions: Background selection is the intentional choice and control of rear-plane environment, color, and detail so scene purpose stays clear.
Control context, brand, and readability of the subject.
rules: Do not use when: Leaving BG to chance on hero frames
decisionRules: Avoid when: Leaving BG to chance on hero frames
examples: Soft branded office bokeh behind interview subject
professionalStandards: Background selection is the intentional choice and control of rear-plane environment, color, and detail so scene purpose stays clear.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Props Selection
items.description: Choosing objects that support story, brand, and product readability.
definitions: Props selection is the curated choice of physical objects that motivate action, signal lifestyle, and reinforce product context.
Add meaning and realism without clutter or brand conflict.
rules: Do not use when: Props that compete with the hero product
decisionRules: Avoid when: Props that compete with the hero product
examples: Morning props: mug, keys, product pouch—only three
professionalStandards: Props selection is the curated choice of physical objects that motivate action, signal lifestyle, and reinforce product context.

sourceMetadata.name: KWIZERA Professional Storytelling & Scene Design Expansion

items.title: Environment Design
items.description: Designing the overall space—architecture, set, location—as a storytelling system.
definitions: Environment design is the holistic crafting of location or set—layout, materials, light logic, and pathways—so scenes feel coherent and brand-true.
Make place express brand world and support blocking.
rules: Do not use when: Run-and-gun docs where environment is found truth
decisionRules: Avoid when: Run-and-gun docs where environment is found truth
troubleshooting: Avoid: Pretty sets that block coverage
examples: Modular kitchen set with clean sightlines for cooking demo
professionalStandards: Environment design is the holistic crafting of location or set—layout, materials, light logic, and pathways—so scenes feel coherent and brand-true.
